one_sentence_story: By pairing optic-chiasm separation with corpus-callosum division at Caltech (1953–1961 Science), Roger Sperry and Ronald Myers solved neurology's biggest riddle — proving the 200-million-fiber corpus callosum transfers perception and memory between hemispheres, and without it two independent learning minds operate inside one skull.
so_what_for_you: Whenever an experiment or audit reports 'changing X made zero difference,' ask Sperry's question: is an unnoticed backup channel (like the optic chiasm!) quietly routing information around your test?

jargon_map.plain: thick bridge of ~200 million white-matter axons linking the left and right cerebral hemispheres
jargon_map.analogy: a transatlantic fiber-optic trunk cable uniting two supercomputers

jargon_map.plain: natural partial crossing of optic-nerve fibers behind the eyes that normally sends half of each eye's view to BOTH hemispheres

jargon_map.plain: complete reset to Trial-1 beginner performance in a split-brain animal the instant an eye-patch shifts from the trained eye to the untrained eye
